cve_summary: The acpi_ps_complete_final_op() function in drivers/acpi/acpica/psobject.c in the Linux kernel through 4.12.9 does not flush the node and node_ext caches and causes a kernel stack dump, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory and bypass the KASLR protection mechanism (in the kernel through 4.9) via a crafted ACPI table.
commit_message:
acpi: acpica: fix acpi parse and parseext cache leaks

I'm Seunghun Han, and I work for National Security Research Institute of
South Korea.

I have been doing a research on ACPI and found an ACPI cache leak in ACPI
early abort cases.

I analyzed this memory leak in detail. I found that “Acpi-State” cache and
“Acpi-Parse” cache were merged because the size of cache objects was same
slab cache size.

I finally found “Acpi-Parse” cache and “Acpi-ParseExt” cache were leaked
using SLAB_NEVER_MERGE flag in kmem_cache_create() function.

When early abort is occurred due to invalid ACPI information, Linux kernel
terminates ACPI by calling acpi_terminate() function. The function calls
acpi_ut_delete_caches() function to delete local caches (acpi_gbl_namespace_
cache, state_cache, operand_cache, ps_node_cache, ps_node_ext_cache).

But the deletion codes in acpi_ut_delete_caches() function only delete
slab caches using kmem_cache_destroy() function, therefore the cache
objects should be flushed before acpi_ut_delete_caches() function.

“Acpi-Parse” cache and “Acpi-ParseExt” cache are used in an AML parse
function, acpi_ps_parse_loop(). The function should have flush codes to
handle an error state due to invalid AML codes.

This cache leak has a security threat because an old kernel (<= 4.9) shows
memory locations of kernel functions in stack dump. Some malicious users
could use this information to neutralize kernel ASLR.

To fix ACPI cache leak for enhancing security, I made a patch which has
flush codes in acpi_ps_parse_loop() function.

I hope that this patch improves the security of Linux kernel.

Thank you.

Signed-off-by: Seunghun Han <kkamagui@gmail.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Completes the final operation in an ACPI parsing state and clears the scope stack.

Parameters: 
WalkState (ACPI_WALK_STATE*): Pointer to the current walk state of the ACPI parser. 
Op (ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT*): Pointer to the parse object representing the operation to complete. 
Status (ACPI_STATUS): The current status of the operation.

Returns: 
ACPI_STATUS: The status of the operation after completion, indicating success or failure.

Logic: 
The function processes the last operation in the parsing state, ensuring that all scopes are terminated cleanly. It checks if the operation is valid and calls the ascending callback if applicable. The function handles control flow based on the status returned from callbacks and manages the completion of each operation in the stack. It continues until all operations are processed, returning the final status.
